newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus plans international shipping conference.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus plans international shipping conference.

text.p: Senior figures from the shipping world will meet in Cyprus for the biennial Maritime Cyprus conference in early October, a local shipping official said on Monday.

Topics ranging from shipping safety and sea pollution, to a forward-looking view of bulk shipping in the next millennium and cruise market trends will be debated at the conference, scheduled to take place in the capital Nicosia between October 6 and 9.

"With a gathering of some 1,000 people it is the largest international shipping conference this year," said Demos Petropoulos, International Relations Officer at the Cyprus Department of Merchant Shipping.

The conference is a joint effort of the ministries of communications and works, the finance ministry, the Central Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Shipping Council, the trade association of the shipping industry on the island.
Cyprus's shipping registry is the fifth largest worldwide, consisting of more than 2,600 vessels in excess of 24 million gross tonnes.

Conference speakers include the Secretary General of the International Maritime Organisation William O'Neil, the chairman of the London-based Baltic Exchange Eric Shawyer, Secretary General of the International Chamber of Shipping and the International Shipping Federation Chris Horrocks, and the Secretary General of the International Transport Workers Federation, David Cockroft.
Conference proceedings have been assigned to mornings only, while Petropoulos said emphasis has been attached to question and answer sessions.
"It is one of the most important aspects of the conference. It is a good opportunity for participants to discuss any queries they may have" Petropoulos told Reuters.
